text.p: Westmoreland Coal Co. said Thursday it was considering filing for bankruptcy in light of unsuccessful talks with the United Mine Workers Pension and Benefit Funds to restructure $160 million in retiree benefit obligations.

"...in light of continued demands and litigation by the funds to force Westmoreland to make payments beyond its financial capacity, the company was examing alternatives, including court protection under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code," Westmoreland said.

"Westmoreland is trying to serve obligations, not escape them," Chairman Christopher Seglem said in a statement. Westmoreland, which moved to Colorado from Philadelphia in 1995, said it is the oldest independent coal producer in the United States at 142 years old.
Westmoreland said it was unable to cover the "enormous" annual cash costs of benefits to the funds' retirees along with its other obligations.
